Cobb County by the numbers

What does the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court record?

Filed here: every Cobb County deed, plat, condominium floor plan, lien, UCC filing, general execution docket entry, military discharge, trade name and partnership. The Real Estate Division is the desk where your deed to a buyer lands, and where the cancellation of your old security deed appears once the loan is paid off.

Find it in Building C at 10 East Park Square in Marietta, beside the State Court Building. Recording is handled upstairs on the second floor and copies in the deed room on the first. Mail goes to P.O. Box 3430, Marietta, GA 30061. Weekday hours start at 8:30 and run until 5:00 in the afternoon, yet the recording and copy counters shut half an hour earlier. The number to call is 770-528-2000.

Because pickup times between the Postal Service and the county mail room have shifted, the clerk asks anyone racing a deadline to mail early and to skip late-afternoon e-filing on the final day.

Who is allowed to file a deed on paper in Cobb County?

Since January 1, 2025, Georgia law under House Bill 1292 requires people filing for themselves to e-file real estate documents. Every person who e-files must first pass identity verification, including a photo check, through the Clerks' Authority portal at efile.gsccca.org. That portal is the only one through which real estate documents can be e-filed.

Paper filing is still open to these groups:

  • Georgia-licensed attorneys
  • Mortgage lenders, whether Georgia licensed or exempt
  • Mortgage servicers
  • Georgia-licensed surveyors
  • Georgia-licensed title insurance companies
  • Georgia-licensed real estate brokers or salespersons
  • Any public official

A member of one of those groups who chooses to e-file has to be verified like anyone else. A seller working through a closing attorney or title company rarely touches the filing, because the closing office submits the deed. An owner who prepares and files a deed without an attorney is the person most affected, and should finish the identity check before the recording date.

How much does the Cobb County clerk charge to record a deed?

A deed costs $25.00 for its first page and nothing for pages after that, according to the schedule the clerk posted for January 1, 2020. Security deeds, assignments, satisfactions and cancellations fall under the same line. An online fee calculator on the clerk's site gives the exact total for a given filing. The counter takes cash, money orders, cashier's checks, certified checks and cards, though a cardholder paying in person must show ID and sign the charge slip.

Selected real estate filing fees posted by the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court
DocumentFirst pageAdded pages
Deeds, security deeds, assignments, satisfactions, cancellations$25.00$0.00
Plats$10.00$10.00
Liens, lis pendens, notices of commencement, fi. fas.$25.00$0.00
State and local tax liens and releases$5.00$2.00
Bonds and landlord bonds$25.00$0.00
Miscellaneous documents$5.00$2.00

Added cancellations, releases, satisfactions and assignments are priced per document in the clerk's schedule. One check can cover the recording fee and the tax, except for trade names. Write it to the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court.

What is the Georgia transfer tax and how is it paid in Cobb County?

Warranty deeds and quit claim deeds both arrive with a PT-61 and the transfer tax, paid when the deed is recorded, unless an exemption applies. The clerk points to O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 and 48-6-2. You fill the PT-61 out online and print it to submit with the deed. Lobby computers let you do that on site.

On its transfer tax page the Department of Revenue states the rate as $1 on the first $1,000 of the sale price, then 10 cents for every further $100, with any fraction counted as a full unit. Liability sits with the seller, though many contracts hand it to the buyer. Your settlement statement shows who paid.

Lenders face a second charge, the intangible recording tax on a long-term note secured by real estate, which the revenue department's fact sheet lists at $1.50 per $500 of the note. The clerk adds that a security deed has to be filed within 90 days of signing to avoid penalty and interest when the note runs past three years or is not exempt. Your buyer's lender cares about that rule far more than you do.

What does a Cobb County deed have to include?

For both warranty deeds and quit claim deeds the clerk lists identical requirements: the full legal description, the name of the party transferring, the name of the party receiving, and the grantor's signature with a witness and a notary. Nobody at the clerk's counter notarizes, so arrive with the deed already done by a commissioned Georgia notary.

The two deed types protect a buyer differently. A warranty deed is the usual choice in a purchase and carries a guarantee that title is good and marketable, which is why buyers and lenders ask for it. A quit claim deed passes only whatever interest the signer holds, with no promise that title is clear or free of liens. It tends to show up in transfers between relatives or into a family entity.

  • Use the full legal description from your last deed, not the street address.
  • Have the notary and the witness sign in the same sitting as the grantor.
  • Complete the PT-61 before you arrive.
  • Bring one payment that covers recording fee and tax.

How do I get copies and check that my old mortgage was cancelled?

Three ways exist to get a recorded document: print it from the clerk's website, copy it in the first-floor deed room, or mail in the request form with a self-addressed stamped envelope. Condo floor plans follow the same routes. After a payoff, the cancellation of a security deed normally goes back to the borrower unless the lender directs it elsewhere, which usually means the mortgage company. You can search the clerk's site to confirm it was filed. Lien payments never go through this office. They go to the lien holder.

Permits for fences, additions and similar work come from another office. The clerk's FAQ sends owners to Cobb County or to the City of Marietta, whichever covers the address.

The clerk's real estate page also links to the Filing Activity Notification System at fans.gsccca.org.

What should a Cobb County seller know about the county itself?

Cobb sits northwest of Atlanta and was carved out of former Cherokee land in 1832. Marietta is the seat and Mableton the largest city. The county spans about 345 square miles, and its 2020 population of 766,149 ranked third in the state. Kennesaw Mountain, the county's high point, rises between Kennesaw and Marietta.

The school district employs more than 15,000 people, the most of any employer, and the county hosts the Home Depot support center, the Weather Channel and the Lockheed Martin plant next to Dobbins Air Reserve Base. Interstates 75, 20, 285 and 575 run through it. The tax commissioner's office bills the county and school district, and the cities of Acworth, Austell, Kennesaw, Mableton, Marietta, Smyrna and Powder Springs bill their own taxes.

Street addresses in the county all count from the southwest corner of the Marietta town square. Liens that must be released before a deed can be recorded are a job for a closing attorney, since the clerk's staff cannot advise you.

More questions about Cobb County, GA Clerk of Superior Court

Which Cobb County office takes a deed for recording?

The Real Estate Division of the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court, in Building C at 10 East Park Square in Marietta. Doors open weekdays at 8:30, the recording counters stop at 4:30 and the office closes at 5:00. Questions go to 770-528-2000.

Can I file my own deed on paper in Cobb County?

Usually not. Since January 1, 2025, people filing for themselves must e-file through efile.gsccca.org after verifying their identity with a photo check. Attorneys, lenders, servicers, surveyors, title companies, brokers and public officials may still file on paper.

What does recording a deed cost at the Cobb County clerk?

Twenty-five dollars for the first page and nothing for added pages, per the clerk's posted schedule. Transfer tax comes on top and is paid with the PT-61. The online fee calculator gives an exact total, and a single check can cover both.

Who owes the transfer tax on a Cobb County sale?

The law puts it on the seller, and the sales contract may move it to the buyer. The Department of Revenue prints the rate as $1 on the first $1,000 of the price plus 10 cents per further $100. Check the settlement statement.

Does the Cobb County clerk notarize or give legal advice?

No on both counts. The clerk's office does not notarize, so bring a deed that is already signed before a notary with a witness. State law also bars the clerk's staff from giving legal advice, so a closing attorney should answer questions about what your deed should say.

Dekalb County by the numbers

What does the DeKalb County clerk's office do at a home sale?

Recording the deed that carries title from seller to buyer falls to the clerk's Real Estate Division, along with mortgages, plats, liens and other papers that touch land in DeKalb County. The office says it receives more than 204,500 real estate documents a year, and its records run back to 1842 because earlier books burned in a fire.

The clerk's FAQ describes three roles: clerk of court, registrar of land records, and collector of intangible and transfer taxes. In practice one office handles the recording, the transfer tax certification and the public index that a title examiner searches before closing.

The Census Bureau counts 267.74 land square miles in DeKalb and estimated 774,394 residents for 2025. The county seat is Decatur.

Where is the Real Estate Division and when is it open?

The division is on the ground floor at 556 N. McDonough Street, Decatur, GA 30030. The real estate page lists 404-687-3812 and weekday hours from half past eight in the morning until five in the afternoon The clerk's general information line is 404-371-2836.

Property records are searchable online through the county's deed search and in the public access room. Searches go fastest when you have three facts in hand:

  • The buyer's name (grantee) and the seller's name (grantor)
  • The year of the transaction
  • The tax parcel ID, which every conveyance filed here must now carry

Copies by mail need the book type and page number, and the office will not process a request without them. Pay by cashier's check, money order or attorney's check made out to the DeKalb County Clerk of Court. Certified copies can also be ordered through the eCertification portal, where an approved request must be paid within six days or it is rejected automatically.

  • Certified copy: $2.50 for the first page, 50 cents for each added page
  • Regular copy: $1.00 per page
  • Plat copy: $2.00 per page
  • Card payments on the fee chart page carry a surcharge of 2% plus $1.00

Can a seller still bring a deed to the DeKalb clerk's counter or mail it?

No. Since January 1, 2025, Georgia House Bill 1292 requires every real estate document in DeKalb County to be filed electronically, and mail-in recording is closed to new filings. The clerk accepts e-recordings from approved providers listed on its page, including Simplifile and CSC.

Anyone who is a party to the instrument and files on their own must also upload a government-issued ID at efile.gsccca.org, where it is verified before the filing can go through. The page cites O.C.G.A. 44-2-39(b)(1) for that step. Most sellers never touch this step, since the firm running the closing e-records the deed. If you are selling without an attorney, such as a family transfer, build the ID check into your timeline.

Plats follow the same electronic rule and have been e-file only since 2017, and UCC financing statements became e-file only in 2022.

What has to be in the package before the clerk will record a deed?

Every deed of conveyance needs a PT-61 transfer tax form and the tax parcel ID printed at the top of its first page. Georgia has required that parcel ID on DeKalb transfers and conveyances since July 1, 2019, under House Bill 694.

The PT-61 is completed online at the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority site, printed, and submitted with the deed. The clerk does not supply forms, the document must be complete before it arrives, and most documents need a signature, a witness and a notary. State identification is required for any filing.

One point sellers like: original documents are recorded immediately and handed back, per the clerk's citation of O.C.G.A. 15-6-72. The recording fee schedule is posted on the clerk's fee page as a Real Estate Fees chart. Georgia moved to flat filing fees in 2020 under House Bill 288, so get the current figure from the clerk or the closing firm instead of an older quote.

How much is the Georgia transfer tax and who pays it?

The seller owes it by law, though a sales contract often shifts it to the buyer. State revenue guidance gives the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 of the sale price, plus 10 cents for each additional $100 or fraction of $100.

Payment comes first; the clerk then attaches a certification that it has been paid. The governing statutes are O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 through 48-6-10. For questions about exemptions, the Department of Revenue points people to the clerk of superior court in the county.

A separate intangible recording tax applies to a long-term note secured by real estate. The state's county facts page puts it at $1.50 per $500 of face value, and in DeKalb the clerk is the collector. A payoff and release on your existing loan is a cancellation of the security deed, and the clerk's page says more than 26,500 mortgages are cancelled in the county each year.

What recording deadlines and rules apply to DeKalb County documents?

Several documents carry a clock that starts when they are signed or when work ends. The clerk's real estate page lists the ones below.

DocumentRule on the clerk's pageAuthority cited
Deed of conveyancePT-61 and parcel ID required; transfer tax due at recordingO.C.G.A. 48-6-1, 48-6-2
Security deedDue 90 days after signing, or penalty and interest on intangible tax when the maturity is over three yearsO.C.G.A. 48-6-61
Foreclosure deedFile within 120 days of signing to avoid a $500 penaltyStated on the clerk's page
Materialmen's or laborer's lienFile within 90 days of the last work or materials; it expires 395 days after filing without a lawsuitO.C.G.A. 44-14-361, 44-14-367
Bond to discharge a lienClerk must approve the bond before it is recordedO.C.G.A. 44-14-364

Table source: DeKalb County Clerk of Superior Court, Real Estate page.

How can a DeKalb homeowner guard against a fraudulent filing?

The clerk participates in the Filing Activity Notification System, called FANS, run through the Georgia clerks' authority at fans.gsccca.org. Owners register their own parcels, or those of relatives, and receive an email when a deed, lien or similar paper is filed or indexed against it. Owners who signed up under the older DeKalb alert system had to register again for FANS.

Before a sale, a forged deed or a surprise lien turns up in the title search and can stall a closing. An alert is cheap protection for an inherited or vacant house. A veteran can also record a DD-214 discharge with the clerk at no charge, which keeps a certified copy on file locally.

What housing numbers frame a DeKalb County sale?

QuickFacts lists 337,059 housing units in DeKalb County in 2025 and 58.8% owner-occupancy for 2020 to 2024. Owned homes had a middle value of $357,800, tenants paid $1,692 in median gross rent, and builders took out 1,321 permits during 2025.

  • Median household income: $80,644 (2020 to 2024, in 2024 dollars)
  • Mean commute: 30.4 minutes
  • Bachelor's degree or higher among adults 25 and over: 47.4%
  • Foreign-born residents: 17.3%

DeKalb was formed in 1822 and lost its western half to Fulton County in 1853. Interstates 20, 85, 285 and 675 cross it, and MARTA rail serves the east and northeast lines. A house in unincorporated DeKalb, in Decatur, in Brookhaven or in Stonecrest all record at the same clerk's office, even though each sits under a different city government.

More questions about DeKalb County, GA Clerk of Superior Court

Must a seller travel to Decatur to file a deed?

No. Real estate documents in DeKalb County must be filed electronically, and self-filers upload a government ID at efile.gsccca.org first. The closing firm usually e-records for a sale.

Which side owes Georgia's transfer tax?

The seller is liable under Georgia law, though the contract can assign it to the buyer. The Department of Revenue rate is $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents per added $100 or fraction of $100, paid before recording.

When must a security deed or foreclosure deed be recorded?

A security deed should be filed within 90 days of signing, and a foreclosure deed within 120 days, which the clerk's page ties to a $500 penalty if missed. Check dates with the closing attorney.

Where can I order a certified copy of a recorded deed?

Order through the eCertification portal, or mail a request listing the book type and page number. The clerk lists certified copies at $2.50 for page one and 50 cents for each added page, and an approved portal order must be paid within six days.

What is a PT-61 and why does the clerk require it?

It is Georgia's real estate transfer tax declaration, completed online and printed. Every deed of conveyance in DeKalb County must carry one, plus the tax parcel ID on page one, before the clerk can record it.
